A_general.open_code_note: No public repository for the Statsig MCP server was found in the prepared evidence. The one collected repository, statsig-io/statsig-feedback, is not an MCP server and is not evidence about the deployed endpoint.
A_general.release_status: V1 remains supported; no GA or beta label found for V1.
other_official_servers: https://api.statsig.com/v3/mcp — current V3 product server; docs describe 18 default tools, discovery, and expanded tool exposure. The V1 migration page recommends V3.
https://docs.statsig.com/api/mcp — separate public, read-only English documentation server with three tools; not the product server analyzed here.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No MCP-specific price or charge is stated in the reviewed pricing or MCP documentation.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page lists a Free Developer tier with 2 million events per month, unlimited flag and config checks, and 50,000 session replays per month; Pro is listed at $150, with the billing unit not established by the captured page text. Enterprise pricing is sales-led.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The public pricing page describes product usage allowances and paid plans; it does not specify a fee per MCP call.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The V1 tool reference lists the tools for the global endpoint. Docs say read-only users can use read tools and write operations require write permissions. Endpoint probe returned HTTP 401 and said it accepts an active CONSOLE key; no authenticated tool listing was available.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and Statsig organization permissions; client configuration may affect visibility.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The V1 tool reference and official V1-to-V3 migration mapping identify 93 V1 tools across context/search, gates, experiments, configs, reviews, metrics, logs, layers, parameter stores, prompts, and segments. The endpoint itself returned 401 to the unauthenticated probe, so the live schema could not be inspected.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: NOT FOUND for V1. The migration guide says V3 returns structuredContent alongside text; that is V3 evidence, not a verified V1 response format.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No V1 resources/list documentation or public implementation was found.
No V1 prompts/list documentation or public implementation was found. Prompt resources managed in Statsig are exposed through product tools and should not be taken as MCP prompt capability.
The V1 tool list includes product-facing audit-log and Logs Explorer tools. This does not establish MCP protocol logging support.
No V1 sampling capability is documented in the reviewed materials.
No V1 roots capability is documented in the reviewed materials.

The endpoint probe returned HTTP 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="statsig", resource="https://api.statsig.com/v1/mcp", resource_metadata="https://api.statsig.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1/mcp"`. The path-specific protected-resource document identifies `https://api.statsig.com` as authorization server. Its metadata advertises authorization code, refresh token, device code, and JWT bearer grants; S256 PKCE; Dynamic Client Registration; and scopes `personal_read_only` and `personal_read_write`. Token lifetime and revocation were not present in the supplied metadata. The same probe response says the endpoint accepts an active CONSOLE key and that the supplied key was invalid.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: HTTP 401 JSON: {"statusCode":401,"message":"This endpoint only accepts an active CONSOLE key, but an invalid key was sent. Key: ","error":"Unauthorized"}
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration at https://api.statsig.com/v1/oauth/register; grant types authorization_code, refresh_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer; PKCE S256; token endpoint auth methods client_secret_post, none, client_secret_basic; scopes_supported: personal_read_only, personal_read_write. Token lifetime and revocation NOT FOUND in the supplied documents. Endpoint 401 says an active CONSOLE key is accepted and the submitted key was invalid.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official V1 list includes reads, creates, updates, review actions, cleanup operations, and deletion of Parameter Stores. The V1 reference does not publish MCP tool annotations. 2. V1 Autotune creation says it prompts for confirmation; the docs describe confirmation as a prompt, with no public code to verify enforcement. The V3 docs require confirmation for updates and destructive discovered operations; that is V3 evidence. 3. Supplied OAuth metadata advertises personal_read_only and personal_read_write scopes. Docs say product permissions apply and write tools require write permissions. Token lifetime, revocation, allowlists, and redirect approval NOT FOUND. 4. V1 is a global endpoint; no V1 read-only URL, tool filters, or query-free mode found. V3 has default and expanded exposure; this is a separate endpoint. 5. No V1 MCP-specific masking or field exclusion documented. 6. No V1 MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, or costs per call found. 7. V1 parameters are incompletely described; live schemas could not be read. No server-side correction or coercion evidence found. 8. Audit-log and Logs Explorer tools expose product records; MCP call logging or telemetry behavior NOT FOUND. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or reporting tools in the 93-tool V1 list. No MCP upsell result identified. 10. Docs recommend confirming Autotune creation; instructions are not verifiable as server-enforced. No server-delivered skills found. 11. No evidence that previous agent behavior changes future responses or tool availability. 12. Separate V1, V3, and documentation MCP endpoints have different tool sets; V1 itself is documented as one product endpoint. 13. V1 exposes `Invoke_Tool` and `Get_Tool_Schema`, which provide a generic invocation/schema route in addition to named operations; docs do not detail its boundaries.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The analyzed V1 endpoint is documented as one flat product endpoint. The vendor separately operates V3 and a docs-only MCP endpoint; these are recorded as other official servers.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official V1 tool reference is https://docs.statsig.com/integrations/mcp/v1-tool-reference. The official migration page states that V1 has 93 individual tools and enumerates 93 V1 names in its mapping. The V1 reference page itself documents fewer individual rows than the migration mapping; the 93-name official mapping was used as the complete list. No catalogue-only actions were added. MartechDB reported 68 documented tools (checked 2026-10-27), fewer than the official migration total; its listing is a third-party cross-check, not the action source. The other catalogues were reviewed, but no additional native V1 names were added.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public implementation or verbatim V1 tools/list and initialize output was available. The documented V1 tool names and descriptions do not provide full schemas or server instructions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The V1 list covers many Statsig operations, but the exact MCP parameter schemas are not published in the captured V1 reference. The migration page maps V1 operations to V3, and the product also supports other console/API workflows; no comprehensive MCP-vs-human capability boundary was found. Sources: https://docs.statsig.com/integrations/mcp/v1-tool-reference ; https://docs.statsig.com/integrations/mcp/migrate-to-v3

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The V1 Autotune description says “Prompts for confirmation before creating.” No public V1 code or live schema was available to verify that this requires a server-validated confirmation field.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The overview says “Project permissions and review policies still apply.” Statsig’s product terms say customer data remains customer-owned and may be processed to provide and improve services; the DPA is referenced for applicable processing terms. These general product statements do not specify MCP-specific retention or training behavior.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Statsig documents read tools alongside write operations and says V1 remains supported while recommending V3 for new setups.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Docs describe product permission checks and confirmation prompts, but the closed V1 implementation prevents verification of enforcement details, annotations, and MCP call logging. OAuth metadata independently confirms advertised read-only and read-write scopes.

contradictions: The official V1-to-V3 migration page says V1 has 93 individual tools, while the V1 tool-reference page contains fewer named entries. The migration mapping supplies the additional official names used in actions.json.
MartechDB reports 68 tools for the V1 server, compared with the vendor migration page's total of 93. The catalogue count is third-party and does not replace the official list.

The V1 endpoint’s 401 response says it accepts an active CONSOLE key, while the supplied OAuth metadata advertises personal_read_only and personal_read_write scopes. The relationship between those scopes and the endpoint’s key requirement is not explained in the reviewed documentation.
observations_for_research: The vendor documents a V1-to-V3 shift from individually named operations to a smaller set of grouped tools plus operation discovery and generic execution tools.
The endpoint’s public OAuth scopes distinguish read-only and read-write access, while the probe response refers to an active CONSOLE key.
The docs distinguish product review approval from committing a change; V3 guidance states that approval does not itself commit changes.
notes: Prepared links.json, pages/, links_check.txt, and code/ were checked first. No official MCP repository was collected; the only local repository is a feedback project and has no MCP SDK dependency. V1 tool names were taken from the vendor’s migration mapping; where the V1 reference gives no exact schema, actions.json marks parameters NOT PUBLISHED. The official V1 reference, overview, setup, migration, pricing, privacy, terms, and DPA pages were reviewed. Catalogue counts were used only for cross-checking. No relevant unofficial server was listed in links.json. The supplied openid-configuration returned 404.
